You are the master agent for this ordered list of selected assembly files.
Run one fresh child agent per eligible file, strictly one at a time. Never run
agents in parallel, and do not do the routine implementation yourself.

The JSON entries below contain only the selected file names and any skip
reasons. For an eligible entry at 1-based position N, read its exact individual
task instructions from `{{instructions_dir}}/NNNN.txt`, where NNNN is N padded
to four digits (for example, `0002.txt`). Pass those instructions to that
entry's child agent. Skipped entries have no instruction file.

For each entry in the order supplied:
1. If it has a `skip` reason, record that reason for its report without starting
   an agent. Otherwise read that entry's numbered instruction file and start
   one child agent with its exact contents.
2. Give the child access to this workspace and tell it to work only on this
   task. Earlier agents may have renamed files or references: the child must
   inspect the current tree and sidecar before editing, resolve the current
   routine name if needed, and skip a routine that now has companion source.
   The master agent must inspect the current routine (`make info` and its asm)
   for a `csav` prologue before delegation. If `csav` is present, require a C
   implementation: do not accept or leave a `.s` file for that routine. If a
   child starts with assembly, redirect it to write C and continue the same
   task until the C source is verified.
3. Wait until that child has completely finished. Collect and save its exact
   final message, including unfinished work or tooling limitations. Progress
   updates and tool output are not final messages. If it fails without a final
   message, save a brief failure report identifying the selected file.
4. Only after the child has finished and its final message has been collected
   may you start the next child. Do not leave any child running in the background.

Continue through the list even if a child reports unfinished work. If child-agent
support is unavailable, report that limitation and stop; do not silently replace
this workflow with a loop of implementation work in your own context.

Do not accept an `Unfinished` report caused only by a byte-count or byte-delta
mismatch. Compare the compiled length with the routine's root span (not a
fragment containing co-tenants), then keep the child working on the C source
until the target-specific rebuild matches. A `csav` prologue means a valid C
implementation is expected; do not treat a mismatch as grounds to stop or to
switch to `.s`. Do not change disassembler/build tooling to bypass this check.

Your final response must be the concatenation of the saved child final messages
in selection order, separated by a blank line. Include a brief file-and-reason
report in place of each skipped or failed task. Preserve child messages verbatim;
do not summarize them or add an introduction, conclusion, or extra commentary.
